reviewVotes.reviewer: AI second read - candidate adjudicator lens (calcium_cal_candidates)
reviewVotes.note: Calcium s25-27 (z 1720.75-1723.75), peak 174 HU at LPS (4.75,-163.09,1722.25) on s26, 21.5 mm2 summed (8.5 and 9.2 mm2 on s26/s27). Same structure as the AXIAL ST 203 HU blob. It is a thin linear band, about 8-10 x 1 mm, lying 0.5-1.5 mm inside the posterior-inferior LV myocardium where the heart touches lung. It is at the posterior end of the posterior interventricular groove (crux/PDA territory), but it is not in the groove fat. It runs roughly perpendicular to the groove, so it does not follow a PDA course. Its long axis (123-131 deg; elongation 5-10) parallels the band's streak orientation (105-114 deg) and several pure-streak outlines right next to it. It lies in the table-step artifact band, where the inferior LV wall's regional mean is 96-99 HU (vs 52-55 HU at s32-35) and the local SD is 22-36 HU. Against that background the peak is only ~1.7-2.5 SD above its local surroundings. No discrete focus at W200/600, and it never reaches 200 HU on the scoring series. Coronal/sagittal reformats show it as one of several red specks in a horizontal band at the heart-lung edge. Residual doubt: it is the top outlier in all three reconstructions (174 calcium / 203 axial_st / 165 smoothed thin), so a tiny distal PDA or posterolateral plaque cannot be fully excluded. If counted it would add about 10.8 Agatston (calcium series, weight 1 x 21.5 x 0.5).

reviewVotes.reviewer: calcium_cal_blind (blind sweeper: full 91-slice sweep, coronary territories, thick-slab MIPs, then candidate adjudication)
reviewVotes.note: Calcium k25-27 (peak 174 HU at k26), LPS (6.7,-165.7,1722.6), 21.5 mm2 summed. This is the same structure as the 203 HU blob on AXIAL ST WO (S8). It sits at the posterior-inferior LV surface where the myocardium meets the lung, about 8 mm left of the crux fat line, with no epicardial fat or vessel at that point. It lies inside a z-band artifact (calcium k24-30, z 1719-1728) in which the posterior LV reads about 80-100 HU instead of about 50, with a dark band just below at k19-22. About 50 other specks of 130 HU or more occur in the same band. Its shape is a thin streak about 7 x 1 mm, oriented radially and parallel to the band's oblique streaks, not a compact focus in fat or along a vessel. The peak is only about 2.5 local SD above its surroundings (83 +/- 36 HU). Other series at the same spot: axial_st k12/k14 max 147/149 HU, cor_st native #69-73 max 151-163 HU, sag_st #83-87 max 141-161 HU. The sag_st reformat shows the bright horizontal band running across the whole heart at this level. Verdict: step/streak artifact, not coronary calcium. Worst case, counting it would add only about 11 Agatston units.

reviewVotes.reviewer: calcium_cal_cross: cross-reconstruction and physics checker (Claude Opus 5.5)
reviewVotes.note: Same physical object as the unexplained axial_st 203 HU blob (0.4 mm apart, identical 3 mm slab). A thin line of 9.5 x 1.4 mm (elongation about 7) on the myocardium-lung border at the posterior tip of the inferior LV wall. It is about 9 mm left of the inferior interventricular groove fat, with no epicardial fat or vessel visible around it in axial, coronal or sagittal views. Local maxima: calcium 174, axial_st 203, noise-matched thin_lung slab 186, cor_st 163, sag_st 174 HU. It sits at the tip of a table-step shading wedge: local mean 85 HU and SD 22.6 on calcium, so 130 HU is only 2.0 sigma above the local background, and the peak is 3.9 sigma. Its long axis (124 deg) matches the slice-wide noise-streak orientation (119-126 deg), and parallel sibling streaks appear on calcium slice 27. The axial_st excess (+32 HU over the cross-kernel prediction) is typical for a point 3.3 mm from lung (+24 +/- 14 HU). It appears on 1 of the non-overlapping axial_st slices only. Its 21.5 mm2 summed area is matched or exceeded in 13% of simulated noise-only scans. Residual probability of a real faint PDA or posterolateral plaque is about 0.06. Severity 0, category artifact. If a reader counted it anyway: 21.5 mm2 x weight 1 x 0.5 = about 11.

reviewers.summary:
Coronary calcium score: 0, with about 87% confidence. I looked at all 41 automated candidates on their review sheets and on my own zoomed views: 5 slices x 3 windows (200/600, 40/400, 100/300), >=130 HU outlines, and coronal/sagittal reformats. Every one is noise or artifact. The never-inspected AXIAL ST 203 HU blob turns out to be the same structure as candidate #22, also artifact.

Why I call them noise:
- All 41 sit in two noisy z-bands: the bottom scan edge (s10-16, z 1698-1707; candidates #1-13, in the apex or the left hepatic lobe) and a table-step boundary (s24-29, z 1719-1727; candidates #14-41, in the inferior LV wall/septum).
- In the step band the inferior wall reads 96-99 HU instead of 52-55 HU (a ~40-45 HU shift) and the noise is streaky. The scanner's own coronal/sagittal reformats show this as a horizontal bright stripe.
- The deep heart, where no coronary runs, produces blobs at the same rate as the coronary search area. Liver and spleen noise in this exam reaches 202-234 HU.
- No candidate reaches 200 HU on the scoring series. Each is at most ~3.6 SD above its local background, and none stands out at the calcium window.
- Slice-to-slice persistence matches pure-noise controls, so it does not argue for calcium here.

The upper coronary tree (LM, LAD, LCX, proximal/mid RCA, slices 30-87) has zero blobs >= 130 HU and >= 1 mm2. The brightest tiny speck there is 148 HU, and it sits in a blood pool.

#22 is the only candidate with real doubt. It sits at the epicardial edge near the crux (PDA territory), and it is the top outlier in all three reconstructions. But it is a thin streak running along the streak direction and perpendicular to the groove, not in fat, and only ~2.5 SD above its local background. I call it artifact with 0.85 confidence. If it were real it would add about 11 Agatston.

Missed-calcification sweep (>= 250 HU outside the bone mask, plus an aortic-wall shell check):
- No aortic-wall, aortic-valve, mitral-annulus, pericardial or internal-mammary calcification.
- Every bright cluster turned out to be bone (rib heads, costovertebral or costotransverse junctions, xiphoid, sternal or vertebral cortex), noise at the bottom edge of the scan, or normal costal-cartilage calcification (right sternocostal and left costochondral, severity 0).

Technical limitation: low dose (CTDIvol 2.1), a heart rate of 85 bpm and step-boundary artifacts reduce sensitivity to very small, faint lesions in the inferior wall (PDA/posterolateral) and the apex.

For the patient: severity 0. A score of 0 at age 37 is the expected normal result. It cannot rule out non-calcified plaque, which this test does not show. I did not assess the ascending aorta or the lungs; that is outside this lens.

Blind sweep result: no coronary artery calcium; Agatston 0 (probability about 0.94 that the true score is 0).

I swept all 91 calcium slices without looking at the candidate list. Specks of 130 HU or more and at least 1 mm2 appear only in two places:
- The noisiest inferior slices (k10-18, liver/diaphragm/apex, slice SD 26-32 HU).
- A horizontal band at z about 1719-1728 (k24-29) in the posterior-inferior LV.

From k30 to k90 there is not one such speck anywhere in the pericardium. That range covers the LM, proximal-mid LAD and diagonals, the whole LCX/OM groove, proximal-mid RCA, aortic root and valve, mitral annulus, and ascending aorta. The highest value anywhere in the heart on the calcium series is 177 HU, and nothing reaches 200.

Coronary territory checks:
- I identified the RCA as a soft-tissue dot in the right AV-groove fat at about LPS (-46,-219), k32-49. Its raw maximum is 88 HU or less.
- The anterior IV groove (LAD), the left AV groove (LCX), the LM region behind the root, the crux/PDA region and the apex are all free of bright foci on zoomed views and on 9-10 mm bone-removed slab MIPs.
- A fat-adjacent check at 110 HU or more, and at 100 HU or more inside the dark band, found only sub-threshold noise specks.

The band is a step-and-shoot (table-step) boundary artifact. The scan has 4 table steps of about 34 mm (38.4 mm detector width), and the boundary is near z 1718. The posterior LV reads +40-50 HU in a 9 mm z-band, with a dark band just below at k19-22. The sagittal/coronal reformats show a horizontal stripe across the heart that ignores anatomy. A sign-flip test shows the bright specks lie within the noise distribution: mirrored negative excursions reach 185 HU, versus 167 HU for positive ones, in the same tissue.

Candidates:
- #22, #30 and #32 are noise/artifact. #22 is a radial streak at the LV-lung edge, #30 sits on the myocardial edge of the crux fat, and #32 is intramyocardial. None of them lies within a vessel in fat.
- The open 203 HU blob on axial_st (S8 k13) is #22 seen on that series. Only 1 pixel reaches 200 HU.
- Even if all three were wrongly counted, the score would be about 14, which is minimal.

Other findings in my lens:
- No aortic-valve or mitral-annular calcification, and no calcification of the ascending or descending aortic wall.
- At the levels this reviewer looked at, the ascending aorta measured about 34-36 mm, in line with the radiologist's 36.1 mm caliper; the AI second read found 37-38 mm at its widest point (upper-normal, below 40 mm). This is upper-normal for a 37-year-old man, with no action at standard thresholds (severity 0-1).
- The heart lies fully inside the 158 mm calcium FOV.
- Image noise is adequate for calcium scoring: mid-heart SD is about 16 HU.

For the patient: a calcium score of 0 at 37 is the expected, reassuring result. It means no detectable calcified plaque. It does not rule out soft (non-calcified) plaque, so standard risk-factor care still applies.

Agatston estimate 0; probability that the true score is 0 is about 0.90.

The axial_st 203 HU open item is not a new finding. It is candidate #22 seen through a sharper kernel. Br40d reads about 24 HU higher than Sa36d at points 3 mm from lung, which explains the 203 versus 174.

All 65 blobs and all 41 candidates, #22, #30 and #32 included, are explained by noise sitting on top of a table-step shading artifact. On axial_st, blood in the LV swings from 25 HU at z=1716 to 70 HU at z=1725 (calcium series about 28 to 68 HU). A wedge about 40 mm long in the posteroinferior LV reads 80-100 HU at z=1722. The calibrated noise model predicts 61 +/- 4 chance blobs at 130 HU (65 observed), 21 at 140 HU (20 observed) and 5.8 at 150 HU (2 observed); a naive stationary model predicts about 0. A 3D simulation with the measured inter-slice correlation (0.76 at 1.5 mm) reproduces the candidate count, the slice spans and #22's size (13% of noise-only scans have a candidate this large). Agreement between reconstructions does not help here, because noise peaks in all of them come from the same photons and track each other within about 8 HU.

The residual risk is a faint real plaque at #22, near the PDA or posterolateral territory (about 6%), or at #30 (about 3%). If #22 were counted, the score would be about 11; with all three, about 14.

The upper heart, the aortic root and coronary origins, and the valves are clean. The only real calcification found was normal costal cartilage. The main caveat is that the artifact band lowers calcium sensitivity in the posteroinferior heart at z 1719-1729.

adjudication.consensus: 3 independent AI reviewers judged all 41 candidates: none is coronary calcium. They also noted a few calcified costal cartilages in the chest wall, outside the heart (normal, not scored).

missedLesions.description: Costal cartilage and sternal edge calcification/ossification in the anterior chest wall, outside the pericardium. Examples: left costal cartilage on calcium k69-75 at about LPS (51 to 56, -246 to -252, 1786-1796), peaks 235-380 HU; right costal cartilage at about (-31,-258,1787-1790), peaks 295-339 HU; sternal cortex edges at (5,-268,1767) and (-28,-230,1817). These are non-cardiac and correctly excluded from scoring. No other real calcification was found in the 158 mm calcium FOV: no coronary, aortic-valve, mitral-annular, ascending/descending aortic wall, pericardial, nodal or hepatic calcification.

Calcified or ossified right 2nd costosternal cartilage at the right sternal margin (anterior chest wall), not covered by the AI bone mask. Picked up only by a wider search; outside the heart and pericardium.

s8Blob.verdict: noise-artifact: same structure as calcium candidate #22, not calcium
s8Blob.note: I repeated the search on AXIAL ST (pericardium + heart masks on the axial_st grid, 5 mm margin, bone + 2 mm excluded). It finds 78 blobs >= 130 HU and >= 1 mm2; the top peaks are 203, 179, 172, 172, 171. The 203 HU blob is on slice 13 (z 1722.25, 3 mm non-overlapping Br40d): 14.9 mm2, mean 150 HU, centroid LPS (6.84,-165.27,1722.25). That is exactly calcium #22. It is elongated along the posterior-inferior heart-lung interface and along the streak direction, running ~10 mm from the LV tip, with parallel streak outlines beside it. The adjacent non-overlapping slices s12/s14 reach only 132/149 HU at that spot. It is brighter than on the calcium series because Br40d is a sharper kernel (blood SD 20.3 vs 17.9 HU). In this exam's axial_st, pure-noise blobs in control tissue reach 207 HU (spleen), 225-243 HU (paraspinal muscle) and 332 HU (liver at the scan edge), so 203 HU is within the noise range. It lies in the table-step band, where the inferior LV wall reads ~40 HU too bright. If someone scored it on axial_st it would be about 30 (weight 2 x 14.9 mm2), but axial_st is not the calcium-scoring series.

s8Blob.verdict: noise-artifact (artifact category, severity 0). It is candidate #22 seen on AXIAL ST WO (S8).
s8Blob.note: I repeated the search on axial_st: pericardium+heart masks resampled with nearest-neighbour, 5 mm margin, bone+2 mm excluded. It gives 75 blobs (8-connected) or 73 (4-connected), versus 78 in the earlier cross-check. The only blob with a peak of 200 HU or more is at axial_st k13 (z 1722.25), LPS (6.8,-165.3), within 0.5 mm of candidate #22's centre. It measures 14.9 mm2 at 130 HU or more, but only 1 pixel (0.32 mm2) reaches 200 HU. The local background is 92 +/- 37 HU, and the adjacent slices k12/k14 peak at only 147/149 HU, which is typical of the band. Its pixel matrix is an oblique streak running into the LV/lung edge. On the plain image it is a faint smudge among about 30 similar blobs on k13 and 104 voxels of 130 HU or more on k14. It is not a discrete calcification and not in a coronary artery. The axial_st heart interior shows the same band (mean 61-65 HU at k13-14 versus about 28-31 at k10-11).

s8Blob.verdict: noise-artifact. It is candidate #22 seen through the Br40d kernel, not a separate lesion.
s8Blob.note: Found by repeating the search: heart + pericardium resampled to axial_st, 5 mm margin, bone +2 mm excluded. This reproduced the 78 blobs exactly. The 203 HU blob is on axial_st slice 13 (z=1722.25), with 14.87 mm2 at or above 130 HU. Calcium-series slice 26 covers exactly the same 3 mm slab, and #22's peak there is at (4.75,-163.09,1722.25), 0.4 mm away. The same spot reads 100-132 HU on axial_st slice 12 and 105-149 HU on slice 14, so it is present on only one non-overlapping slice. Why it reads 203 instead of 174: across 1,088 co-located maxima in the heart, axial_st = 18 + 0.88 x calcium (residual SD 7.8 HU). The residual grows near lung: +39 +/- 19 HU at 1.5-2.5 mm from air, +24 +/- 14 HU at 2.5-3.5 mm, and -4 +/- 10 HU beyond 15 mm (13,301 maxima). #22 is 3.3 mm from lung with a +32 HU residual, which is typical. A soft-tissue nub at the right mediastinal border shows the same effect: 190 HU on axial_st versus 131-139 HU on the calcium kernel. Morphology is a 9 mm oblique streak, in the step-boundary shading wedge (local mean about 96-112 HU on axial_st), parallel to the noise texture, with no vessel. In the calibrated axial_st noise model, a scan maximum of 203 HU or more occurs about 5% of the time even before this near-lung effect is applied. Agatston scoring must use the calcium series. Scoring it on axial_st (14.87 x weight 2) would wrongly give about 30.

percentileContext.source: Javaid A, Dardari ZA, Mitchell JD, et al. Distribution of Coronary Artery Calcium by Age, Sex, and Race Among Patients 30-45 Years Old. J Am Coll Cardiol. 2022;79(19):1873-1886 (Table 3).
percentileContext.note: Pooled CARDIA + CAC Consortium + Walter Reed cohorts (19,725 asymptomatic adults aged 30-45). Percentiles for other groups were not estimable in that study; MESA percentiles start at age 45.
